summary:
SIDEREA is a student-led aerospace research project focused on Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-Ocular Syndrome (SANS), a condition involving changes in astronauts’ eyes and vision during or after long-duration spaceflight.
Our proposed solution is PHOTON, a modular binocular ocular-monitoring concept supported by a digital research platform.
It aims to bring together:
• Real scientific imaging: OCT, fundus photography, MRI and ultrasound research.


• Research data: Published NASA and scientific-study findings.


• AI-assisted analysis: Experimental image assessment and measurement support.


• Longitudinal monitoring: Organising and comparing eye-related data over time.


• A research platform: Connecting images, measurements, astronaut profiles and mission timelines in one place.


Our mission: To make spaceflight ocular-health research more connected, accessible and organised, helping researchers better understand how spaceflight affects human vision.
SIDEREA is a proposed student research system, not a clinically validated scanner or diagnostic medical device.
details:
SIDEREA — Project Details
SIDEREA is an aerospace medical research project focused on protecting astronauts’ eye health during long-duration space missions.
Our project addresses Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-Ocular Syndrome (SANS), which can cause changes in astronauts’ eyes and vision due to the effects of microgravity.
Our solution is PHOTON — a proposed advanced binocular ocular-monitoring system connected to a digital research platform.
We aim to combine optical imaging, real scientific data, eye tracking, AI-assisted analysis and longitudinal monitoring in one integrated system.
What makes SIDEREA different is that we don’t just want to capture images; we want to connect the images, understand the changes and make the research easier to analyse.
Our vision is to take one step closer to protecting human vision beyond Earth.
